title.narrative: WFAD: Friska unga - friska samhällen: Att omvandla våldsamma ungdomar i Kinshasa
WFAD: Sober Youth - Healthy Communities: Transforming Violent Youth in Kinshasa

description.narrative: Svenska ambassaden i Kinshasa har ett avtal med World Federation against Drugs (WFAD) om projektet Friska unga – friska samhällen: Att omvandla våldsamma ungdomar i Kinshasa. Projektet syftar till att förebygga ungdomsvåld i Kinshasa och WFDA arbetar med fyra projektimplementerande partnerorganisationer.

The Swedish Embassy in Kongo-Kinshasa, has an agreement with the WFAD (World Federation against Drugs) concerning a project “Sober Youth – Healthy Communities: Transforming Violent Youth in Kinshasa”. The project aims to prevent youth violence in Kinshasa and WFAD works with four project implementing partners.

The general objective of this contribution is to prevent young people from joining, and support others in leaving, the street gangs, whilst contributing to a strengthened drug policy in the country. In order to prevent and tackle urban violence, this intervention will introduce and support mechanisms for mentoring and empowering young people through psychosocial support, vocational training, entrepreneurship, socio-economic and social reintegration, for the positive development of youth in becoming contributing members of the community. Moreover, the capacities of partner organisations and network of organisations and stakeholders working against the social and socio-economic consequences of alcohol and drug use in the DRC will be strhengthened, and regional cooperation to share best practices will be developed to advocate for and create better preconditions to prevent youth from joining, and support others in leaving violent street gangs. As far as the theory of change is concerned, WFAD suggests a four levels of intervention to meet the needs of these young people: individual, family, community and institutional levels. The project will offer support in recovery and desistance from violence, criminal behaviour and illicit drug use, including parental support groups, and provide vocational training as well as income generating activities. Advocacy activities targeting key institutional stakeholders, including local authorities, police, and policymakers will enable the enhancement of credibility, cooperation between different actors/stakeholders. As well as possibility for replication and mainstreaming of the activities. The project offers a clear environmental dimension as it focuses on sanitation services and production of clean and affordable water, while offering clear gendered specific support.

description.narrative:
Overall, the project achieved satisfactory results, delivering a positive and significant transformation for its beneficiaries.
WFAD continued to mentor and support 30 young men who had received theoretical training in agriculture and fish farming in 2024, with this support extending into 2025. These young men were assigned to the Kimwenza farm for practical training, which we had the opportunity to visit.
They are engaged in subsistence farming, providing short-term income, and our visit was greatly appreciated. During our discussions, we observed that they were full of confidence. Many had never realized that subsistence farming could meet their financial needs. At the time of our visit, they were harvesting eggplantsa vegetable in high demand in Kinshasa. They explained that they harvest eggplants every three months and then weekly for three to four consecutive months. Each harvest yields two baskets of eggplants, sold at $10 per basket. This generates approximately $160 per month, with additional income from other vegetables and fish farming.
One of the main challenges to overcome is the complexity of transporting produce to marketa distance of over 100 km on poorly maintained dirt roads where transportation is scarce.
As the project concludes, WFAD has planned to organize the young men into groups of 10, rotating every two weeks so they can continue cultivating crops on the projects plots. Two small houses built on-site will serve as accommodation, along with a kitchen and storage spaces for produce and seeds.
It is worth noting that the projects partnership with Equity Bank BCDC continued with these 30 young men. They received training in financial literacy and entrepreneurship to equip them with the necessary tools to manage their production with an entrepreneurial mindset.
WFAD will continue to seek funding to consolidate the projects achievements and replicate the youth mentoring program in other cities such as Lubumbashi, Goma, and Kongo Central, where youth violence is widespread due to high unemployment.
Finally, WFAD concluded the project with its implementing partners. The transfer of equipment was completed, and the vehicle will be handed over to the NGO SYFES. In collaboration with the NGO DASOD, well management systems were established with neighborhood leaders to ensure the sustainability of two drilled wells. Inter Action will retain all sanitation equipmentincluding motorcycles, tricycles, and two trucksto continue their valuable work with youth in the community.
The project remains to be finalized, which involves tracking unspent funds that WFAD must return to Sida, as well as the interest generated.
